name: Third War
summary: Across Lordaeron and Kalimdor, the Third War ended only after mortals stood against the Burning Legion. The war began with the Lich King's Plague of Undeath and brought down Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas before the defense of Mount Hyjal.

sections.title: The Plague and the Prince
sections.body:
The Third War began with plague in northern Lordaeron. Infected grain from Andorhal carried a sickness that killed its victims and raised them as ghouls bound to the Lich King's will. Prince Arthas Menethil and Jaina Proudmoore, a sorceress of the Kirin Tor, tried to stop it.

Dreadlords turned Arthas's grief and fear toward Stratholme. He purged its infected people, then pursued his foe to Northrend. There Arthas took Frostmourne, the cursed runeblade, and cast aside his soul. He returned south and murdered his father, King Terenas. Lordaeron then fell into the Scourge's hands.

sections.title: The Invasion of the Legion
sections.body: Arthas used the dead to crush Quel'Thalas and raise the necromancer Kel'Thuzad at the Sunwell. The Scourge then besieged Dalaran and seized the spellbooks needed to summon Archimonde, the demon lord, into Azeroth. With Archimonde on mortal soil, Dalaran was leveled by arcane devastation. The Scourge had served as the Legion's advance guard. Now the Burning Legion turned toward the eternal power across the Great Sea.

sections.title: The Flight West and Mount Hyjal
sections.body:
The mysterious Prophet sent cryptic warnings to Warchief Thrall and Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Thrall led the New Horde across the Great Sea, while Jaina brought surviving Alliance refugees to safety. In ancient Kalimdor, the newcomers clashed with the reclusive night elves.

Then the three factions recognized the threat before them. Atop Mount Hyjal, mortals joined forces beneath the World Tree Nordrassil. When Archimonde reached the tree, ancestral wisps destroyed him. The Legion's vanguard was broken, and the war ended.

sections.title: A Scarred World
sections.body:
Archimonde's fall brought no lasting peace. Lordaeron's Alliance is gone. Stormwind and Ironforge now anchor the southern Alliance, while the old kingdom rots as the Plaguelands. In Kalimdor, Thrall's Horde has carved out Durotar, though tensions with the newly allied night elves remain volatile.

The Scourge still holds the northern ruins. The freed undead, called the Forsaken, hold the catacombs of Capital City. They fight to survive against their former masters and vengeful crusaders.

faq.q: When did the Third War happen?
aliases: how long ago was the war
faq.answer: The Third War began when the Plague of Undeath broke out in Lordaeron and ended at the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The devastation is only four years past, so ruins are fresh and nearly every adult alive fought in the war or lost family to it.

faq.q: How was the Third War different from the First and Second Wars?
aliases: difference between third war and second
faq.answer: The First and Second Wars were chiefly struggles between the Old Horde and the Alliance kingdoms. The Third War brought a demonic invasion that shattered nations. Mortals fought the Burning Legion and its undead Scourge across three continents, forcing enemies into a desperate truce.

faq.q: What happened to the Kingdom of Lordaeron?
faq.answer: Lordaeron was destroyed from within. The Cult of the Damned tainted the regional grain with the Plague of Undeath, killing people and raising them as monsters. Prince Arthas fell to corruption, murdered his father King Terenas II, and delivered the broken kingdom to the Scourge.

faq.q: Who was the Prophet that warned everyone to go to Kalimdor?
faq.answer: The Prophet was Medivh, the Last Guardian of Tirisfal. Seeking atonement for opening the Dark Portal, he traveled as a raven-cloaked wanderer. He warned that Lordaeron was doomed and urged its leaders to unite in Kalimdor.

faq.q: Why are the night elves part of the Alliance now?
aliases: why did night elves join alliance
faq.answer: The night elves had lived in strict isolation for ten thousand years. The Third War brought the Legion back to their sacred forests and made them sacrifice their immortality to slay Archimonde at the World Tree. In a changed world, with resource conflicts growing between them and Thrall's Horde and Scourge corruption still present, they left their solitude and allied with the races of the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: How did the Horde escape the war in Lordaeron?
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall trusted Medivh's prophetic dreams. He rallied the freed clans from the internment camps, raided human ports for sailing ships, and crossed the Great Sea before the Scourge or Legion fully consumed Lordaeron.

angles.text: Lordaeron's fall moved Alliance leadership south to Stormwind and Ironforge. Survivors look north, longing to reclaim their homeland.
For Thrall's Horde, the war brought redemption. Grommash Hellscream slew Mannoroth and broke the demonic blood curse, so the orcs could build a sovereign nation in Kalimdor.
The Forsaken are Lordaeron's people, slain by the plague and forced to serve the Scourge. They broke free and claimed the Undercity.
Defending Nordrassil cost the kaldorei their immortality. It also opened their ancient homelands to the wider world for the first time in ten thousand years.
The Knights of the Silver Hand were torn apart in the war. Arthas disbanded them, murdered Uther the Lightbringer, and turned their holy halls into charnel houses.
